page0.text:
We get away from Fuji-nee in the living room and resume our meeting from earlier on the porch.
We've been debating since noon, so I throw all my weight into it, expecting that we won't be able to reach a conclusion that easily, but...

page1.text:
"It's impossible to challenge Ryudou Temple at this moment.
The only thing we can do is set up a trap and lure Caster out."
Tohsaka starts with the solution.

page2.text:
"...Well. You're right, but..."
"The problem is what to do for the trap.
...Well, I have two or three possible ideas, so you can stand by for now. In the worst case, I'll have you and Saber be bait."

page3.text:
She says something dangerous like that and opens the exterior sliding door.
The cold air comes in.
But this porch must be special, as it's only slightly chilly.
...The same as that night five years ago.
This porch is the only place warm enough to be able to watch the moon even during the winter.

page4.text:
"...The Bounded Field you have is nice. I feel some human emotion, unlike the one at my place."
She sits down on the porch and stares into the yard.
"Can you keep me company for a bit? I just want to talk."

page5.text:
...
I silently sit down next to her.
Tohsaka said she has something to talk about, yet she doesn't say anything.
There's nothing to do, so I just stare blankly at the yard.

page6.text:
...
I can't see the moon.
My breath is white. It was cold enough to snow a little.
When I look to Tohsaka, she's peering out over the yard, her breath white as well.

page7.text:
...
Our shoulders will touch if I move a little.
I'm oddly no longer flustered by the closeness.
Maybe I've gotten used to it. Or the magic of this winter night has been cast.
The girl I admire so much is so close, yet I'm strangely calm.

page8.text:
"...What did you want to talk about, Tohsaka?"
I felt like she wanted to ask me something, so I ask her.

page9.text: "...Well, there's something about this place. I find myself thinking that maybe you don't have to learn like that. I suppose, well, it might be you're just fine the way you are."

page10.text:
"Wait, are you saying I'm fine staying an amateur?"
"Not exactly, but I guess...
I don't know what kind of mage Kiritsugu Emiya was, but this house feels real naturalistic. It's very open even though it's a mage's workshop.
All the doorways are open, and you can enter and exit as you please. It's probably not restricted by anything since there's no knowledge to protect."

page11.text: "I think that's what your father meant when he told you to be someone who uses magecraft rather than to be a mage. You don't have anything, but in return, you can go anywhere."

page12.text:
"What, is it not like that for you?"
"No, my place is different. People call my mansion a haunted house, but it's actually true. It rejects anybody that approaches, yet it doesn't release anyone that comes in."

page13.text:
"...Sometimes I think it's not right, but I can't change it.
It's not like it's cursed, and I like how it is myself. I was chosen as the successor because of my personality, but I was pretty surprised when I realized it."

page14.text:
"...Hm. So you mean when you realized you were a bully?"
"...I've been thinking this, but you don't mince your words, do you?"
"Really? I thought I snuck it in real well, like you do."
"...Ugh, I saw it coming a mile away."

page15.text:
She sighs and her head droops down.
The white residue of her breath slowly melts in the cold night.

page16.text:
...I steal a glance at her side profile and remember.
The red school.
Tohsaka didn't say anything seeing the students that collapsed from Rider's doing.
She put a brave face on like always, while her knees shook and she bit her lip.

page17.text:
...That's when I realized.
The more she acts like a perfect mage, the more it's like she's killing her true self.

page18.text:
"Was it hard for you, Tohsaka?"
I get uneasy and ask.

page19.text:
"You mean the training? Sorry, but I never thought so. I was able to do most things easily. I've never felt daunted by anything since everything always came so easily.
Besides, it was fun to learn new things. I told you, right? I was born with this personality. So there's no need for you to worry."

page20.text:
She tells it as she sees it.
There is no bluster or lies that I can make out. Instead, I just see a wonderful smile.

page21.text: "Okay. Then what about school? If you're going to live as a mage, then isn't it pointless to go to school?"

page22.text:
"It's not pointless, but it is a detour.
I wouldn't say it's a waste, though. Being a student is fun. I suppose you could say I'm an Epicurean. It's my duty to succeed my father, but I wouldn't do even that if wasn't fun.
I became a Master because I wanted to test my own powers, and I'm working with you because you're funny."

page23.text:
...
Putting her opinion that I'm funny to the side, that takes weight off my shoulders.

page24.text:
A family of mages.
I thought that Tohsaka was burdened with a dark and heavy shadow because she's bound to a long history and bloodline.
But I guess I don't really have a clue about that sort of thing.
The Tohsaka family is not a burden or anything to her, and she's been doing what she wants freely.

page25.text:
"...I see. I'm glad you're having fun."
"Thanks. So you're the same if you're saying that, right? You wouldn't be able to continue training if you weren't having fun."
I suppose that would be the natural conclusion.
However...
"Hm..."
I find myself unable to nod in agreement.

page26.text: "...Hey, why are you being quiet? Your father didn't force you, right? But you continued in spite of that, so wasn't it because magecraft was fun?"

page27.text:
"Uh, well..."
I have never once felt that it was fun.
Magecraft has always been a dangerous trial to me.

page28.text:
I know that I don't have the aptitude.
Even so, in my desperation to be like Kiritsugu, I've clung onto it.

page29.text:
For my first year, other than when I slept or ate, I spent all my time on training.
Facing death every night, I honed my sensitivity.
And I repeated that for eight years.
I didn't think it was tough, but I didn't think it was fun.

page30.text:
"...Hold on. Answer me, Emiya.
I might have the wrong idea here."
Tohsaka glares at me seriously.

page31.text:
"..."
...I'm stuck.
If she makes a face like that, I can't not answer.

page32.text: "...Yeah. I've never thought that magecraft is fun. I've never thought that training is fun. But so long as others around me are happy, I'm happy too. So I thought that I could be of help to someone if I learned magecraft."

page33.text:
...
"I wanted to be a hero of justice like Kiritsugu. That's why I've been learning magecraft. I thought I could do right if I did."

page34.text:
"...So what? You didn't learn magecraft for your own sake?"
"Huh? ...Well, isn't this for my own sake? I'm glad if I can be of help to someone."

page35.text:
"Hey now. You're glad, but not having fun!
Listen, what I mean is what's in it for you. I'm not asking about the others; I'm asking about you. What you enjoy.
Tohsaka's practically roaring.

page36.text:
...
Even if she says that, I can't answer.
I can't think of anything that's fun for me, and most of all...
...I don't have the right to have such a desire.

page37.text:
"That makes me mad! You care too much for others to care about yourself!"
Tohsaka suddenly stands and points at me.

page38.text:
"Huh? Wait, Tohsaka, your finger...!"
Her finger, no, her nail is digging into the tip of my nose!

page39.text:
"Shut up! Don't talk back to me. Ugh, I thought that you two are alike, but I didn't think you were this similar!"
She rejects my objection and closes in on me even more.

page40.text:
"Hold on. Calm down, Tohsaka. Why are you so mad?"
"I'm pissed off since you can't tell! Dammit, why did no one tell you!?"
Her fist shakes.

page41.text:
...
All I can do is stay quiet.
I can only do as Tohsaka says until her anger subsides.

page42.text:
...Then...
After she vents all her anger...
"...Humph. Fine, I've decided.
I'll make you admit defeat tomorrow."
She says, as if smacking me with a glove.

page43.text:
"...That's ominous. Are we going to continue our fight?"
It goes without saying that I'm referring to our bout at school.
I was cornered and about to surrender, but we weren't able to settle the score since Rider interrupted.

page44.text:
"That's right, you just wait and see. I'll give you a taste of something special I've been saving!"
Tohsaka psyches herself up before walking off towards the living room.

page45.text:
"...Hm."
I don't know what's going to happen.
Am I supposed to be ready for anything...?

page46.text:
Anyway, I have to take Tohsaka home.
It's almost 10 PM.
I don't know what Fuji-nee will say if I keep a girl out this late.

page47.text:
"Huh? What did you just say, Shirou?"
"I said I'm going to take Tohsaka home... But, where is she anyway? It's not good if she doesn't go home already."

page48.text:
Fuji-nee is looking at me, stunned.
...That's strange.
I thought Fuji-nee would approve right away, but she doesn't particularly seem to be in a rush.

page49.text:
"Hmm. I think Tohsaka is in the outbuilding.
She's a guest, so she has to have a proper guest room if she's going to stay over."
"All right, the outbuild—No, wait, are you pulling something, Fuji-nee? What'd you just say?"

page50.text:
"You're the one trying to pull something.
You're going to have Tohsaka stay over since it's late, right? Tohsaka just came and told me so."
"Wha—Tohsaka is staying over...!?"

page51.text:
"Yes? And, so we're clear, you won't do anything to her, okay?
I'll be sleeping in the other room, so if I hear a scream from the guest room, your ass is grass and I'm the lawn mower."

page52.text:
Fuji-nee munches on rice crackers.
She acts normal, as if she thinks nothing of the emergency she's describing.

page53.text:
"That girl...!"
It looks like Fuji-nee has already surrendered to Tohsaka.

page54.text:
"Oh, good timing. I'm going to borrow the guest room on the right."
Then...
I run into an alien while on my way to the outbuilding with the guest rooms.

page55.text:
"Huh? Oh..."
Her appearance makes my head spin.
Tohsaka is in her own clothes, not her uniform.
And she's in the hallway of my house saying something crazy.

page56.text: "Oh, this? I decided to sleep over, so I had Archer bring me things I need. And I won't need to borrow pajamas."

page57.text:
"Uh... Uh?"
"Hey, are you okay? You should go to bed early if you're tired. I won't forgive you if you sleep in tomorrow morning."
She waves and disappears into the hallway that leads to the outbuilding.

page58.text:
I dumbfoundedly see her off, then glance at the mirror in the hallway.
"..."
My face is as red as an apple.
...Damn it.
What is she thinking, sleeping in the same house? Even if we are still technically pretty far apart...

page59.text:
"...Maybe I'll go take a bath again."
I'll pour cold water over myself and cool my burning face.
...Um, I feel like I have to do so or else Tohsaka's image will be stuck in my head, and I won't be able to focus on my training...
